title: Ottawa Ankle & Foot Rules — X-ray Decision
subtitle: acute ankle/midfoot injury · casualty

sources.title: STG & EML Primary Healthcare, 8th ed. 2024 (updated Sept 2026)
Stiell IG et al. Ottawa ankle rules. JAMA 1993;269:1127-32; JAMA 1994;271:827-32

left.title: Ankle X-ray series if malleolar-zone pain AND any of

steps: A — bone tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of the LATERAL malleolus (distal 6 cm)
B — bone tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of the MEDIAL malleolus (distal 6 cm)
Unable to bear weight (4 steps) both immediately after injury and in casualty

left.title: Foot X-ray series if midfoot pain AND any of

steps: C — bone tenderness at the base of the 5th metatarsal
D — bone tenderness at the navicular
Unable to bear weight (4 steps) both immediately after injury and in casualty

items.label: All negative
items.t: Fracture very unlikely (sensitivity ≈98–99%) — no X-ray; treat as sprain
Intoxication, head injury, multiple injuries, reduced sensation in the leg
Injury >10 days old, or re-assessment of a known injury
Children: validated from about 5 years; use with caution
Minor injuries (incl. sprains) are managed as outpatients — exclude fractures
Sprain: immobilise with a firm bandage and/or temporary splint; analgesia
